title: Spiced Minced Beef Keema with Peas
changes_from_base: Frozen peas stirred in for the last 3 min; otherwise the same spice base and method.
summary: Keema matar follows the classic keema method and spice base, with frozen peas stirred in for the final 3 minutes for sweetness and colour. Serve with warm rolls, rice or chapatis.
equipment: large saucepan or deep frying pan (24-28 cm) with lid

ingredients.item: large red onion, halved and thinly sliced
fine sea salt or table salt
Kashmiri chilli powder (or 1.5 tsp sweet paprika plus a pinch of cayenne)

steps.title: Bloom whole spices
steps.text: This is the classic keema with peas added at the end. Warm the oil in the saucepan over medium heat, add the peppercorns, cardamom and cinnamon and stir for 30 seconds until they smell fragrant; the hot oil draws out their flavour.

steps.title: Colour the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and stir it often for 8-10 minutes until it turns a deep brown. The caramelised onion gives the sauce its sweet, savoury backbone.

steps.title: Brown the mince
steps.text: Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the mince and salt. Over medium-high heat, cook for 8-12 minutes, breaking the meat up finely, until the juices have evaporated, it sizzles and the pan base looks dry and browned. Once the water is gone the meat can brown, which builds flavour.

steps.title: Toast the spice powders
steps.text: Sprinkle in the coriander, chilli powder, turmeric and cumin and keep stirring for 1 minute so they lose their raw edge in the hot fat.

steps.title: Cook down the sauce
steps.text: Mix in the tomatoes, yoghurt and green chilli and bring to a simmer. Put the lid on and cook over low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring from time to time, until the tomatoes have collapsed and a spoon pulled through leaves a clean trail. Make sure a thermometer in the keema shows at least 71 °C.

steps.title: Add the peas
steps.text: Stir in the frozen peas and simmer for 3 minutes until hot and bright green. Adding them late keeps them sweet and vivid instead of dull and mushy.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Take out the cinnamon stick and cardamom pods if you prefer, fold in most of the coriander and finish with the garam masala and the rest of the coriander. Serve with the warm rolls and lime wedges.

tips: A common mistake is adding the peas too early; they lose their colour and sweetness, so stir them in only for the last 3 minutes.
There is no need to thaw the peas first; they go straight from the freezer into the pan.
Make sure the mince is properly browned before adding the spices for the fullest flavour.
A squeeze of lime just before eating brightens the rich sauce.
storage: Cool within 2 hours and refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot (74 °C).
